key_points.text: AI delivers extraordinary efficiency gains — up to 176% on digital tasks and 56% faster coding — but without a deliberate system for reclaiming the hours saved, those gains vanish into more work rather than buying you time.

segments.text: The productivity industry has a dirty secret. A Stanford study found generative AI makes people up to 176% more efficient on digital tasks. A joint study by MIT Sloan, Microsoft Research, and GitHub clocked a 56% reduction in programming time. So why do you feel busier than ever?

A 2026 Harvard Business Review analysis by Berkeley's Aruna Ranganathan argues that without deliberate systems, AI doesn't reduce work — it intensifies it. The gains are real. The recovery is not automatic.

I'm James Harrington. McKinsey's superagency framework shows that AI can repurpose time for personal fulfilment, but only when workflows are deliberately redesigned. Benjamin Laker, writing for MIT Sloan Management Review, describes how to identify the high-compression, low-judgement tasks AI should handle, reserving your hours for what requires genuine judgment.

That is the difference between a tool that accelerates your treadmill and one that buys you back your time. Subscribe, and I'll show you how to build the system that ensures AI saves your time — not steals it.
